claims.evidence_paraphrase: Hubert's protected identifier points to H G Morrison Junior, while the adjacent H. G. row carries a different rank and protected identifier.

claims.temporal_assessment: The records establish a wartime identity conflict and do not establish any pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Phoebe Morrison is a high-confidence match to the Yale international lawyer documented in OSS Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An FTC oral-history witness worked for Phoebe Morrison in OSS and identified her as an international lawyer who came from Yale; Hoover preserves her 1945 OSS memo.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact name, explicit OSS workplace testimony, Yale continuity, and an item-level OSS archival record.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish Yale work before the documented OSS role, but not the exact recruitment date or an uninterrupted transition.
claims.match_notes: The claim does not rely on a discovery-only biographical profile or infer intervening employment.

claims.claim_text: Phoebe Morrison held documented prewar employment at Yale's law school, identified as an assistant professor in 1939 and Research Associate in International Law in 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary newspaper named her as a Yale law-school assistant professor; the 1941 book title page identified her as Yale's Research Associate in International Law.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact name and independent Yale-to-OSS identity evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment. The sources do not prove Yale was the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The two contemporaneous titles are preserved; no exact start or end date is inferred.
